newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke sees some leeway with EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke sees some leeway with EMU criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday that there is some leeway in interpreting the two fiscal criteria that nations need to meet to join Europe's planned currency union.
"There is discretionary leeway in interpreting the two fiscal criteria for EMU and they are greater than often reported," Welteke told an audience.
Welteke said the fiscal criteria, which demand that a nation avoids excessive public decficits, "should be seen as based on the broad economic situation."

Fielding a barrage of questions on how the criteria will be applied when political leaders review 1997 data to determine which country will enter the currency union in 1999, Welteke said the leeway for interpretation was in place. By simply pointing this out, the Bundesbank was in no way advocating any softning of criteria.

"The Treaty for the currency union only forbids excessive deficits, but the reference values that a deficit should not exceed three percent of gross domestic production and government debt should not exceed 60 percent of gross domestic product are already enshrined in the Treaty on Europe's economic union," Welteke said.
Welteke said emotional discussions about the fiscal criteria may actually obscure the broad spirit of the currency union, demanding nations practice fiscal austerity in the long run.
Reaching the targets exactly may not actually be meeting the Treaty in spirit he said, adding: "In some cases, having a budget deficit of three percent to gross domestic product is far too much.
"We want to achieve sustainable fiscal austerity and that doesn't necessarily need to be 63 percent," Welteke said trying to illustrate there was some leeway.
At the same time, Welteke sought to calm fears that Germany may agree to softening the criteria and allowing countries that are not ready to join the union.
"I am only arguing that the fiscal criteria be interpreted as they are laid down in the Treaty," Welteke said, adding that these criteria should not be over-interpreted.
